title: Failed encrypted exports may leave a plaintext archive
description: The authenticated export route writes a ZIP to the final export path before optional encryption. Errors after that write are returned without removing the archive. Whether another principal or a sync/backup reader can access it is unknown.
claimed_root_cause: Password-protected export stages plaintext at the final path before encryption, so a later failure may leave an unencrypted archive there.

trace.description: After route authorization, the request body and optional password are passed to exportSnapshots.
The ZIP is written at the final path before encryption, and the catch does not remove that path.

evidence.description: The export route calls the authorization helper before handling the request.
The catch returns an error without deleting the archive.
writeZip renames its temporary file to the requested path.

blockers: Failure-path plaintext residue was not reproduced because the required OS-enforced sandbox is unavailable.
Effective export directory permissions and any other principal, sync, or backup reader are not established.
Whether real snapshots contain sensitive values depends on local state that was not inspected.

validation_plan.local: When compliant sandboxing is available, use a temporary export root and synthetic snapshot with a dummy marker; inject a failure after the final ZIP write and before encrypted replacement, then inspect only that dummy file and remove the fixture.
validation_plan.deployment: Have the owner inspect the effective export directory permissions and configured sync/backup scope without opening real export contents.
